historical_references.reference: The name 'Shaqr' is mentioned in the historical account of the Battle of Hunayn in 630 AD, which took place shortly after Muhammad's migration from Mecca to Medina. This battle secured control of the Arabian Peninsula for the Muslim forces and marked the end of the Ridda Wars.
historical_references.context: Battle of Hunayn and the Ridda Wars

historical_references.reference: The name 'Shaqr' also appears in the biography of Ibn al-Hanafiyya, a prominent figure during the Second Fitna (Civil War) in Islamic history. He led a major rebellion against Umar II, the Caliph at that time, and was known as 'Abu al-Ash'ath al-Shaqr'. The name 'Shaqr' is believed to have been given to him due to his lean and emaciated appearance.
historical_references.context: Second Fitna and the rebellion of Ibn al-Hanafiyya
